market.summary: The morning gap-up did not hold: the Sensex fell for a fourth day and the damage was in mid and small caps (Smallcap 100 -2.9%), with only about 1 in 10 NIFTY 500 stocks rising. Oil near $111-116 on new Middle East attacks and a weaker rupee keep the regime RISK-OFF. After the close Infosys cut its FY27 growth guidance, which weighs on IT sentiment on Monday. For the open trades this means small/mid-cap holdings (SEJALLTD, THELEELA, GROWW) are being sold with the market rather than on company news.

points.text: Sensex -125.56 (-0.17%) to 73,123.83, its fourth fall in a row; Nifty -0.39% to about 22,600; Nifty Midcap 100 -2.21%, Smallcap 100 -2.94%; India VIX +6%. Metals, realty and PSU banks were weakest, IT held up best.
NIFTY 500 breadth: 50 advances vs 450 declines; only about 22% of tracked stocks are above their 21-day EMA.
NSE provisional flows 23 Oct: FIIs net bought about Rs 888 Cr and DIIs about Rs 3,235 Cr; over 5 sessions FIIs are still net sellers of about Rs 1,531 Cr.
Rupee near 94.92 per dollar, giving back its weekly gain; a drone attack on a Saudi oil field and US staff withdrawals from the Gulf keep a risk premium in oil.
US Friday midday: Dow -0.9%, S&P 500 -0.1%, Nasdaq +0.3% after Thursday's chip sell-off; the US 10-year yield is back below 5%; Brent near $111.
Infosys (after the close): Q2 FY27 net profit +6.2% YoY, but FY27 constant-currency revenue guidance cut to 1-2% from 1.5-3%, citing pricing pressure; large deals $5.2 bn.

market.watch: Monday: how IT reacts to the Infosys cut, whether small caps stabilise, Brent above $110, and the Fed meeting on 28 Oct.

INDHOTEL.summary: Bought today after a strong result: IHCL raised its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 15-17% and brokers lifted targets (HSBC 910, Goldman 890, Macquarie 860). The stock held flat at about 782 on a day when mid caps fell over 2%, which is the kind of relative strength the PEAD drift needs.
